You have to consider the statement and the following assumptions and decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement. Statement: One can customize Dell laptop if they want as per their needs. Assumptions: 1. They want to increase their customer base throughout the world. 2. They want to prove they are the best company for laptops.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Given below is a statement followed by two assumptions numbered 1 and 2. You have to consider the statement and the following assumptions and decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.

Statement: One can customize Dell laptop if they want as per their needs.

Assumptions:

1. They want to increase their customer base throughout the world.

2. They want to prove they are the best company for laptops.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Option 1".

Given:

Statement: One can customize Dell laptop if they want as per their needs.

Assumptions:

I. They want to increase their customer base throughout the world - True (Because offering laptop customization is a customer-oriented feature. It is reasonable to assume that such a feature is introduced to attract and retain more customers, thereby expanding the company's customer base.)

II. They want to prove they are the best company for laptops - False (Because the statement only informs customers about the availability of customization. It does not require the assumption that Dell is trying to establish itself as the best laptop company.)

So, only Assumption I is implicit.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question: Ranjan in his ODI Cricket career, scored 15 runs on an average in 10 matches. If he scored 14 runs on an average in the first 4 matches and 12 runs on an average in the last 4 matches, then find the average of the runs scored by him in the remaining 2 matches.
questions.questionHtml: Ranjan in his ODI Cricket career, scored 15 runs on an average in 10 matches. If he scored 14 runs on an average in the first 4 matches and 12 runs on an average in the last 4 matches, then find the average of the runs scored by him in the remaining 2 matches.
questions.solution:
• Average runs in total 10 matches = 15

∴ sum of runs in total 10 matches = 15 × 10 = 150. 

  • Average runs in first 4 matches = 14

∴ sum of runs in first 4 matches = 14 × 4 = 56. 

  • Average runs in last 4 matches = 12

∴ sum of runs in last 4 matches = 12 × 4 = 48. 

  • Sum of runs in the remaining 2 matches = total runs in 10 matches - (sum of runs in first 4 matches + sum of runs in last 4 matches)

∴ sum of runs in remaining 2 matches = 150 - (56 + 48) = 150 - 104 = 46.​

⇒ average of runs in remaining 2 matches = 46 ÷ 2 = 23

Hence, the correct answer is "23".

questions.question: Which of the statements given below with reference to the Morley-Minto reforms of 1909 are correct? 1. It introduced a form of responsible government in India. 2. Morley-Minto reforms gave the people of the country a shadow rather than substance. 3. It sowed the seed for the partition of India. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the statements given below with reference to the Morley-Minto reforms of 1909 are correct?

1. It introduced a form of responsible government in India.

2. Morley-Minto reforms gave the people of the country a shadow rather than substance.

3. It sowed the seed for the partition of India.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 and 3 only.Key PointsEvaluation of Morley-Minto Reforms, 1909:

  • It was made obvious by Lord Morley that India was not a good candidate for colonial self-government.
  • He opposed the formation of an accountable government in India. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
  • The reforms actually sought to use separate electorates as a tool to restrain the growing unity of Indians.
  • The acceptance of separate electorates laid the foundation for the partition of India.  Hence, statement 3 is correct.
  • The election process was too indirect.
  • They were elected by the electoral college which was elected by local bodies.
  • No responsibility was conceded while parliamentary forms were introduced. 
  • These reforms gave the people a shadow rather than substance. Hence, statement 2 is correct.

Additional Information

The following are some reasons why the Act of 1909 was significant:

  • This enabled the first election of Indians to the country's numerous legislative councils.
  • The establishment of the electoral concept provided the foundation for a parliamentary system.
  • It first acknowledged the elective principle as the foundation for the composition of the legislative council.
  • It provided Indians with other channels through which to express their complaints.
  • Additionally, they have the chance to criticise the executives and offer suggestions for more effective management.
  • The Act increased Indian participation in the legislative councils, especially at the provincial level.
  • Members may move motions and talk about the budget. Additionally, they could ask follow-up questions.
  • The first Indian to serve on the Viceroy's Executive Council was Satyendra P. Sinha, who was nominated by Lord Minto.
  • The Secretary of State's Council on Indian Affairs received two nominations from Indians.

  • It is defined as the amount of substance that contains exactly 6.02214076 × 1023 elementary entities (e.g., atoms, molecules, ions, or electrons). This number is called the Avogadro constant.
  • One mole of any substance contains the same number of particles as there are atoms in 12 grams of pure carbon-12.
  • The mole provides a link between the macroscopic scale (mass in grams) and the microscopic scale (number of particles).
  • It is widely used in chemistry, physics, and material sciences to quantify the amount of a chemical substance.

Additional Information

  • Avogadro's Constant:
    • Avogadro's constant (6.02214076 × 1023 mol-1) is a fundamental physical constant that specifies the number of particles in one mole of a substance.
    • It is named after the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro, who first hypothesized the concept.
  • Relationship Between Mole and Molar Mass:
    • The molar mass (in grams per mole) of a substance is numerically equal to the relative atomic or molecular mass of the substance.
    • For example, 1 mole of water (H2O) has a molar mass of 18 g/mol.
  • Applications of the Mole Concept:
    • Used to calculate the amount of reactants and products in a chemical reaction.
    • Helps in determining concentrations in solutions (e.g., molarity).
  • Other Related SI Units:
    • Kelvin (K): Measures temperature.
    • Pascal (Pa): Measures pressure.
    • Siemens (S): Measures electrical conductivity.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a bacterial disease?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is not a bacterial disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Asthma.

  • Asthma is not a bacterial disease.
  • Asthma is a condition in which your airways narrow and swell and may produce extra mucus.
  • Asthma can make breathing difficult and trigger coughing, a whistling sound (wheezing) when you breathe out, and shortness of breath.

Key Points

  • Asthma signs and symptoms are:
    • Shortness of breath.
    • Chest tightness or pain.
    • Wheezing when exhaling, which is a common sign of asthma in children.
    • Trouble sleeping caused by shortness of breath, coughing or wheezing.
    • Coughing or wheezing attacks are worsened by a respiratory virus, such as a cold or the flu.
  • Types of Asthma are:
    • Allergic asthma: Allergens trigger this common type of asthma.
    • Nonallergic asthma: Irritants in the air not related to allergies trigger this type of asthma.
    • Occupational asthma:  Occupational asthma is a type of asthma induced by triggers in the workplace.

Additional Information

Disease Details
Typhoid

Typhoid is a bacterial infection that can lead to a high fever, diarrhoea, and vomiting.

It can be fatal. It is caused by the bacteria Salmonella typhi.

The infection is often passed on through contaminated food and drinking water, and it is more prevalent in places where handwashing is less frequent.
Plague

Plague is an infectious disease caused by Yersinia pestis bacteria, usually found in small mammals and their fleas.

The disease is transmitted between animals via their fleas and, as it is a zoonotic bacterium, it can also transmit from animals to humans
Diphtheria

Diphtheria is a serious infection caused by strains of bacteria called Corynebacterium diphtheriae that make toxins (poison).

It can lead to difficulty in breathing, heart failure, paralysis, and even death.

CDC recommends vaccines for infants, children, teens, and adults to prevent diphtheria.

questions.question: Kapil travelled a certain distance by a bus travelling at a speed of 25 km/h and then came back on foot at a speed of 4 km/h. The entire journey took 5 hours and 48 minutes. What is the distance travelled by Kapil by bus?
questions.questionHtml: Kapil travelled a certain distance by a bus travelling at a speed of 25 km/h and then came back on foot at a speed of 4 km/h. The entire journey took 5 hours and 48 minutes. What is the distance travelled by Kapil by bus?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a certain distance is covered at speeds S1 and S2 and total time T is given:

Distance = [ (S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2) ] × T

⇒ Total Time T = 5 hr 48 min = 5 + (48 ÷ 60) = 29 ÷ 5 hours

⇒ Distance = [ (25 × 4) ÷ (25 + 4) ] × (29 ÷ 5)

⇒ Distance = (100 ÷ 29) × (29 ÷ 5) = 100 ÷ 5 = 20

∴ The correct answer is 20 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed by bus (S1) = 25 km/h

Speed on foot (S2) = 4 km/h

Total time (T) = 5 hours 48 minutes = 5 + (48 ÷ 60) = 5 + (4 ÷ 5) = 29 ÷ 5 hours

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Time = T1 + T2

Calculation:

⇒ Let the one-way distance be D km.

⇒ Time taken by bus = D ÷ 25 hours

⇒ Time taken on foot = D ÷ 4 hours

⇒ (D ÷ 25) + (D ÷ 4) = 29 ÷ 5

⇒ (4D + 25D) ÷ 100 = 29 ÷ 5

⇒ 29D ÷ 100 = 29 ÷ 5

⇒ D = (29 × 100) ÷ (29 × 5)

⇒ D = 100 ÷ 5 = 20

∴ The correct answer is 20 km.

Additional Information

Average Speed Formula

When equal distances are covered at speeds S1 and S2, the average speed for the entire journey is (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

Time Difference Formula

If the difference in time taken to cover a distance D at two speeds S1 and S2 is Δt, then Distance D = [ (S1 × S2) ÷ |S1 − S2| ] × Δt.

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S1 − S2|). In opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S1 + S2).

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 1368 and their HCF is 171. Find all possible pairs of such numbers.
questions.questionHtml: The sum of two numbers is 1368 and their HCF is 171. Find all possible pairs of such numbers.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of co-prime ratio parts = Total Sum ÷ HCF

⇒ Sum of parts = 1368 ÷ 171 = 8

Possible co-prime pairs summing to 8 are (1, 7) and (3, 5).

Multiply each part by the HCF (171) to find the original numbers.

⇒ Pairs = (171 × 1, 171 × 7) and (171 × 3, 171 × 5).

∴ The correct answer is (171, 1197) and (513, 855).

Alternate Method

Given:

Sum of two numbers = 1368

HCF of the numbers = 171

Calculations:

⇒ Let the two numbers be 171x and 171y, where x and y are co-prime to each other.

⇒ Sum of the numbers = 171x + 171y = 1368

⇒ 171 × (x + y) = 1368

⇒ x + y = 1368 ÷ 171

⇒ x + y = 8

⇒ The possible pairs of co-prime integers (x, y) whose sum is 8 are (1, 7) and (3, 5).

Note: (2, 6) and (4, 4) are not co-prime pairs because their HCF is greater than 1.

⇒ When (x, y) = (1, 7), the numbers are (171 × 1, 171 × 7) = (171, 1197).

⇒ When (x, y) = (3, 5), the numbers are (171 × 3, 171 × 5) = (513, 855).

⇒ Hence, the possible pairs of numbers are (171, 1197) and (513, 855).

∴ The correct answer is (171, 1197) and (513, 855).

Additional Information

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime if their highest common factor (HCF) is 1. This means they do not share any common prime factors.

Representation of Numbers using HCF

Any two numbers can always be written in the format Hx and Hy, where H is their HCF and x, y are strictly co-prime integers.

LCM and HCF Relationship

The product of any two given numbers is exactly equal to the product of their LCM and HCF. Formula: N1 × N2 = LCM × HCF.

questions.question: If (x + \(\frac{1}{x}\) ) = \(\frac{11}{5}\) , what is the value of (x 3 + \(\frac{1}{x^3}\) )?
questions.questionHtml: If (x + \(\frac{1}{x}\)) = \(\frac{11}{5}\), what is the value of (x3 + \(\frac{1}{x^3}\))?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula: If x + 1/x = a, then x3 + 1/x3 = a3 − 3a

Here, a = 11/5

x3 + 1/x3 = (11/5)3 − 3 × (11/5)

x3 + 1/x3 = 1331/125 − 33/5 = (1331 − 825) / 125

x3 + 1/x3 = 506/125 = 4 6/125

∴ The correct answer is 4 6/125.

Alternate Method

Given:

x + 1/x = 11/5

Formula Used:

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

Calculations:

⇒ Cubing both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (x + 1/x)3 = (11/5)3

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 + 3 × x × 1/x × (x + 1/x) = 1331/125

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 + 3 × 1 × 11/5 = 1331/125

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 + 33/5 = 1331/125

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 1331/125 − 33/5

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 1331/125 − (33 × 25) / (5 × 25)

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = (1331 − 825) / 125

⇒ x3 + 1/x3 = 506/125 = 4 6/125

∴ The correct answer is 4 6/125.

Additional Information

Higher Power Algebraic Identities

If x + 1/x = a, the square relation is x2 + 1/x2 = a2 − 2, and the fourth power relation is x4 + 1/x4 = (a2 − 2)2 − 2.

Negative Form Algebraic Identities

If x − 1/x = a, the square relation is x2 + 1/x2 = a2 + 2, and the cube relation is x3 − 1/x3 = a3 + 3a.

questions.question: 3 ten rupees coins of diameter 2 cm are placed on a table such that all of them touch each other. The area enclosed by all 3 coins is:
questions.questionHtml: 3 ten rupees coins of diameter 2 cm are placed on a table such that all of them touch each other. The area enclosed by all 3 coins is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The direct formula for the area enclosed by 3 identical circles of radius r touching each other is r2(√3 − π/2).

Given the diameter of each coin is 2 cm, the radius (r) = 1 cm.

Enclosed Area = (1)2 × (√3 − π/2) = (√3 − π/2) cm2.

∴ The correct answer is (√3 − π/2) cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of each coin = 2 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 1 cm.

When three equal circles touch externally, their centers form an equilateral triangle.

Side of the equilateral triangle (a) = r + r = 1 + 1 = 2 cm.

Formula Used:

Area of Equilateral Triangle = (√3/4) × a2

Area of a Sector = (θ/360°) × πr2

Calculations:

⇒ Area of the equilateral triangle formed by the centers = (√3/4) × (2)2 = √3 cm2.

⇒ The internal angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, meaning the coins form three 60° sectors inside the triangle.

⇒ Total area of the 3 sectors = 3 × (60°/360°) × π × (1)2

⇒ Area of the 3 sectors = 3 × (1/6) × π = π/2 cm2.

⇒ Enclosed Area = Area of Equilateral Triangle − Area of 3 Sectors

⇒ Enclosed Area = (√3 − π/2) cm2.

∴ The correct answer is (√3 − π/2) cm2.

Additional Information

Area Enclosed by 4 Touching Circles

If four identical circles of radius r touch each other externally, their centers form a square of side 2r. The enclosed central area is calculated as r2(4 − π).

Length of a Belt Around 3 Circles

The exact length of a rubber band or belt tightly stretched around three identical touching circles of radius r is given by the formula 2πr + 6r.

Equilateral Triangle Properties

questions.question: Anjali decided to spend 45% of her salary on shopping. On completion of her shopping, she realised that she had spent only ₹11,475, which was 60% of what she had decided to spend. How much is Anjali's salary?
questions.questionHtml: Anjali decided to spend 45% of her salary on shopping. On completion of her shopping, she realised  that she had spent only ₹11,475, which was 60% of what she had decided to spend. How much is Anjali's salary?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net percentage of salary actually spent = 60% of 45% = 27%.

Given that 27% of Salary = ₹11,475

1% of Salary = 11,475 ÷ 27 = 425

100% of Salary = 425 × 100 = 42,500

∴ The correct answer is ₹42,500.

Alternate Method

Given:

Percentage of salary planned for shopping = 45%

Amount actually spent = ₹11,475

Percentage of planned amount actually spent = 60%

Formula Used:

Actual Amount = Total Salary × (Planned Percentage ÷ 100) × (Actual Spend Percentage ÷ 100)

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total salary of Anjali be S.

⇒ Planned spending amount = 45% of S = (45 ÷ 100) × S = 0.45 × S

⇒ Actual spending amount = 60% of planned amount

⇒ Actual spending amount = 60% of (0.45 × S)

⇒ Actual spending amount = (60 ÷ 100) × 0.45 × S

⇒ 0.60 × 0.45 × S = 11,475

⇒ 0.27 × S = 11,475

⇒ S = 11,475 ÷ 0.27

⇒ S = 1,147,500 ÷ 27

⇒ S = 42,500

∴ The correct answer is ₹42,500.

Additional Information

Successive Percentages

When a value undergoes consecutive percentage changes, the net effect can be calculated by multiplying their fractional equivalents. Final Net Percentage = 100% × (x/100) × (y/100).

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Converting percentages to fractions simplifies complex calculations quickly without decimals: 45% = 45 ÷ 100 = 9/20, and 60% = 60 ÷ 100 = 3/5. Therefore, actual spend = (9/20) × (3/5) = 27/100 = 27%.

Base Value Formula

To find the original base amount when the final value and overall percentage rate are given, use the formula: Base = (Final Value × 100) ÷ Percentage Rate.

questions.question: Deepak starts a business with a capital of ₹1,60,000. He incurs a loss of 10% during the first year. But he makes a profit of 5% during the second year on his remaining investment. Finally, he makes a profit of 25% on his new capital during the third year. Find his total profit at the end of three years.
questions.questionHtml: Deepak starts a business with a capital of ₹1,60,000. He incurs a loss of 10% during the first year. But he makes a profit of 5% during the second year on his remaining investment. Finally, he makes a profit of 25% on his new capital during the third year. Find his total profit at the end of three years.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Successive multiplying factor = (90/100) × (105/100) × (125/100)

Final Amount = ₹1,60,000 × (9/10) × (21/20) × (5/4)

Final Amount = ₹1,60,000 × (945/800)

Final Amount = ₹200 × 945 = ₹1,89,000

Total Profit = Final Amount − Initial Capital = ₹1,89,000 − ₹1,60,000 = ₹29,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹29,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Capital (P) = ₹1,60,000

Loss in 1st year = 10%

Profit in 2nd year = 5%

Profit in 3rd year = 25%

Formula Used:

Final Amount = P × (1 − L/100) × (1 + P1/100) × (1 + P2/100)

Total Profit = Final Amount − Initial Capital

Calculations:

⇒ Amount after 1st year = 1,60,000 × (1 − 10/100)

⇒ Amount after 1st year = 1,60,000 × (90/100) = ₹1,44,000

⇒ Amount after 2nd year = 1,44,000 × (1 + 5/100)

⇒ Amount after 2nd year = 1,44,000 × (105/100) = ₹1,51,200

⇒ Amount after 3rd year = 1,51,200 × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ Amount after 3rd year = 1,51,200 × (125/100) = ₹1,89,000

⇒ Total Profit = Final Amount − Initial Capital

⇒ Total Profit = 1,89,000 − 1,60,000 = ₹29,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹29,000.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value experiences continuous sequential changes, the net resultant value is determined by continuously multiplying the base amount with successive fractional factors: Final = Base × (1 ± r1/100) × (1 ± r2/100).

Equivalent Percentage Change

For two consecutive percentage changes of a% and b%, the combined overall percentage effect can be strictly derived from the direct formula: Net Change = (a + b + ab/100)%. In this formula, instances of decline or loss must be appropriately noted as negative quantities.

Compound Interest Analogy

The arithmetic principle of determining consecutive profits or losses computed on a continually updated principal is structurally identical to the framework of Compound Interest, wherein accrued amounts inherently form the foundation for the next interest period.

questions.question: The tax value of an article is Rs 800. After allowing a discount of 12% on its marked price, it is sold for Rs 844.80. If it is sold at a discount of 12.5% ​​on the same marked price, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: The tax value of an article is Rs 800. After allowing a discount of 12% on its marked price, it is sold for Rs 844.80. If it is sold at a discount of 12.5% ​​on the same marked price, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Selling Price (SP) at 12% discount = 88% of Marked Price (MP) = ₹844.80

New Selling Price at 12.5% discount = 87.5% of MP

New SP = (844.80 ÷ 88) × 87.5 = 9.6 × 87.5 = ₹840

Profit = New SP − Cost Price = 840 − 800 = ₹40

Profit % = (40 ÷ 800) × 100 = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) = ₹800 (Note: 'Tax value' is a literal translation of 'kraya mulya' which means Cost Price)

Selling Price 1 (SP1) = ₹844.80

Discount 1 (D1) = 12%

Discount 2 (D2) = 12.5%

Formula Used:

Marked Price (MP) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − D%)]

Selling Price (SP) = MP × [(100 − D%) ÷ 100]

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ First, find the Marked Price (MP) using the initial Selling Price.

⇒ MP = 844.80 × [100 ÷ (100 − 12)]

⇒ MP = 844.80 × (100 ÷ 88)

⇒ MP = ₹960

⇒ Now, calculate the new Selling Price (SP2) at 12.5% discount.

⇒ SP2 = 960 × [(100 − 12.5) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP2 = 960 × (87.5 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP2 = 960 × (7 ÷ 8) = 120 × 7 = ₹840

⇒ Calculate Profit on the new Selling Price.

⇒ Profit = SP2 − CP = 840 − 800 = ₹40

⇒ Profit % = (40 ÷ 800) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP) & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d1% and d2% are given, the equivalent discount is [d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2) ÷ 100]%.

Relation between CP and MP

The direct ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is given by: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

questions.question: If P gets 10 percent more marks than Q, then by what percentage marks of Q are less than the marks of P?
questions.questionHtml: If P gets 10 percent more marks than Q, then by what percentage marks of Q are less than the marks of P?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If a value A is R% more than B, then B is [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100% less than A.

Here, R = 10.

Required % = [10 ÷ (100 + 10)] × 100

Required % = (10 ÷ 110) × 100 = 100 ÷ 11 = 9.09%

∴ The correct answer is 9.09%.

Alternate Method

Given:

P gets 10% more marks than Q.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the marks obtained by Q be 100.

⇒ Marks obtained by P = 100 + 10% of 100 = 110.

⇒ Difference in marks between P and Q = 110 − 100 = 10.

⇒ We need to find by what percentage marks of Q are less than P. Here, the base value for comparison is P's marks (110).

⇒ Required Percentage = (Difference ÷ Marks of P) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (10 ÷ 110) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 100 ÷ 11 = 9.09%

∴ The correct answer is 9.09%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change is calculated as: [(Difference) ÷ Base Value] × 100. The base value is always the quantity with which the comparison is being made (the one that comes after the word "than").

Base Shift Rule

If quantity A is x% more than quantity B, then B is less than A by exactly [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100%.

Common Percentage Fractions

Memorizing standard fractions saves calculation time: 1/9 = 11.11%, 1/11 = 9.09%, 1/8 = 12.5%, 1/12 = 8.33%.

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 35%, 10% and 30% in three successive months, but increases by 65% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price?
questions.questionHtml: The price of fuel decreases by 35%, 10% and 30% in three successive months, but increases by 65% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price?
questions.solution:

Price after 4th month: 40.95 × (1 + 65 ÷ 100) = 40.95 × 1.65 = 67.5675

Overall percentage change: ((67.5675 − 100) ÷ 100) × 100 = −32.43%

questions.question: A spherical ball of radius 27 m is melted into 27 smaller spherical balls of radius (R) m. What is the value of R?
questions.questionHtml: A spherical ball of radius 27 m is melted into 27 smaller spherical balls of radius (R) m. What is the value of R?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a large sphere is melted into N identical smaller spheres, the relation between their radii is directly derived from the cube root of N.

Formula: Rlarge = Rsmall × 3√N

Substituting the given values: 27 = Rsmall × 3√27

⇒ 27 = Rsmall × 3 ⇒ Rsmall = 9 m

∴ The correct answer is 9 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the larger spherical ball (R1) = 27 m

Number of smaller spherical balls (n) = 27

Let the radius of the smaller ball be R.

Formula Used:

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r3

When melted and recast: Total Initial Volume = Total Final Volume

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of larger ball = 27 × Volume of one smaller ball

⇒ (4/3) × π × (27)3 = 27 × (4/3) × π × R3

⇒ (27)3 = 27 × R3

⇒ 19683 = 27 × R3

⇒ R3 = 19683 ÷ 27

⇒ R3 = 729

⇒ R = 3√729

⇒ R = 9 m

∴ The correct answer is 9 m.

Additional Information

Volume and Surface Area of Sphere

For a sphere of radius r: Volume = (4/3)πr3 and Total Surface Area = 4πr2.

Melting and Recasting Rule

When a solid shape is melted and cast into another shape, the total volume always remains perfectly constant regardless of the change in physical dimensions or total surface area.

Similar 3D Objects Property

If two objects are perfectly similar in shape, the ratio of their volumes is equal to the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions (e.g., V1/V2 = r13/r23).

questions.question: A train runs at a speed of 90 km/h in the first 10 min, 60 km/h in the next 20 min, and 40 km/h in the last 5 minutes. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the train?
questions.questionHtml: A train runs at a speed of 90 km/h in the first 10 min, 60 km/h in the next 20 min, and 40 km/h in the last 5 minutes. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the train?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Average speed can be calculated directly by taking the weighted average of speeds using their respective time ratios.

Time ratio (t1 : t2 : t3) = 10 : 20 : 5 ⇒ 2 : 4 : 1

Average Speed = (v1t1 + v2t2 + v3t3) ÷ (t1 + t2 + t3)

⇒ Average Speed = (90 × 2 + 60 × 4 + 40 × 1) ÷ (2 + 4 + 1)

⇒ Average Speed = (180 + 240 + 40) ÷ 7 = 460 ÷ 7 = 65 5/7 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 65 5/7 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Speed 1 = 90 km/h, Time 1 = 10 min = 10/60 hr = 1/6 hr

⇒ Speed 2 = 60 km/h, Time 2 = 20 min = 20/60 hr = 1/3 hr

⇒ Speed 3 = 40 km/h, Time 3 = 5 min = 5/60 hr = 1/12 hr

Formula Used:

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Calculations:

⇒ Distance D1 = 90 × (1/6) = 15 km

⇒ Distance D2 = 60 × (1/3) = 20 km

⇒ Distance D3 = 40 × (1/12) = 10/3 km

⇒ Total Distance = 15 + 20 + 10/3 = 35 + 10/3 = (105 + 10) / 3 = 115/3 km

⇒ Total Time = 1/6 + 1/3 + 1/12 = (2 + 4 + 1) / 12 = 7/12 hr

⇒ Average Speed = (115/3) ÷ (7/12) = (115/3) × (12/7)

⇒ Average Speed = (115 × 4) ÷ 7 = 460 ÷ 7 = 65 5/7 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 65 5/7 km/h.

Additional Information

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed can be directly calculated using the formula 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

For three equal distances covered at individual speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is given by 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed Concept

If two bodies move in opposite directions, their effective relative speed is (V1 + V2). If they move in the same direction, it is (V1 − V2).

questions.question: A train crosses a 1000 m long bridge in 52 seconds and another 700 m long bridge in 40 seconds. Assuming the train is running at a uniform speed, what is the speed (in km/h) of the train?
questions.questionHtml: A train crosses a 1000 m long bridge in 52 seconds and another 700 m long bridge in 40 seconds. Assuming the train is running at a uniform speed, what is the speed (in km/h) of the train?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When a train crosses two objects of different lengths, Speed = Difference in length ÷ Difference in time.

⇒ Speed = (1000 − 700) m ÷ (52 − 40) s

⇒ Speed = 300 ÷ 12 = 25 m/s

⇒ Speed in km/h = 25 × (18 ÷ 5) = 90 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 90 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of first bridge = 1000 m, Time taken = 52 s

Length of second bridge = 700 m, Time taken = 40 s

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Distance covered to cross a bridge = Length of Train + Length of Bridge

Calculations:

Let the length of the train be L meters and speed be S m/s.

⇒ Total distance to cross 1000 m bridge = L + 1000

⇒ Total distance to cross 700 m bridge = L + 700

Since the speed is uniform, we can equate the speeds (S = D ÷ T):

⇒ (L + 1000) ÷ 52 = (L + 700) ÷ 40

Cross multiplying the equation:

⇒ 40 × (L + 1000) = 52 × (L + 700)

⇒ 10 × (L + 1000) = 13 × (L + 700)

⇒ 10L + 10000 = 13L + 9100

⇒ 13L − 10L = 10000 − 9100

⇒ 3L = 900

⇒ L = 300 m

Now, substitute the value of L in the speed equation:

⇒ S = (300 + 700) ÷ 40

⇒ S = 1000 ÷ 40 = 25 m/s

To find the speed in km/h, multiply by 18/5:

⇒ Speed in km/h = 25 × (18 ÷ 5) = 90 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 90 km/h.

Additional Information

Crossing a Platform / Bridge

When a train crosses a stationary object with length (bridge, platform, tunnel), Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Object.

Crossing a Pole / Man

When a train crosses a pole, a standing man, or a tree, Total Distance = Length of the Train itself.

Unit Conversion Rule

To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5. To convert from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18.

questions.question: A, B and C can do a work separately in 20, 35 and 60 days, respectively. They started the work together, but B and C left 8 days and 12 days, respectively, before the completion of the work. For how many days, did all three work together?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can do a work separately in 20, 35 and 60 days, respectively. They started the work together, but B and C left 8 days and 12 days, respectively, before the completion of the work. For how many days, did all three work together?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Work = LCM(20, 35, 60) = 420 units | Efficiencies: A = 21, B = 12, C = 7.

If B and C stayed till the end, additional work = (12 × 8) + (7 × 12) = 96 + 84 = 180 units.

Total time to finish work = (420 + 180) ÷ (21 + 12 + 7) = 600 ÷ 40 = 15 days.

Since C left 12 days before completion, C worked for 15 − 12 = 3 days, which is the exact duration all three worked together.

∴ The correct answer is 3 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A alone = 20 days

Time taken by B alone = 35 days

Time taken by C alone = 60 days

B left 8 days before completion and C left 12 days before completion.

Concept / Formula Used:

Total Work = LCM of given individual times.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 20 420 21
B 35 12
C 60 7

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total time to complete the work be x days.

⇒ A worked for the entire x days.

⇒ B worked for (x − 8) days.

⇒ C worked for (x − 12) days.

⇒ Total work = Work done by A + Work done by B + Work done by C

⇒ 420 = 21x + 12(x − 8) + 7(x − 12)

⇒ 420 = 21x + 12x − 96 + 7x − 84

⇒ 420 = 40x − 180

⇒ 40x = 600

⇒ x = 15 days

⇒ The work was completely finished in 15 days.

⇒ Since C left 12 days before the completion, C worked for 15 − 12 = 3 days.

⇒ All three worked together only as long as C was present, which means they worked together for exactly 3 days.

∴ The correct answer is 3 days.

Additional Information

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If individuals work for the same total duration, wages are divided strictly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the total work done in a complete cycle (e.g., A + B combined over 2 days) and approach the total work using multiples of this cycle period.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept remains fundamentally identical to Time and Work. The only specific variation is that an emptying pipe (outlet) possesses a negative efficiency, while a filling pipe (inlet) possesses a positive efficiency.

questions.question: A 70 cm wide path is made around a circular garden having a diameter of 14 metres. What is the area of the path (in m 2 )?
questions.questionHtml: A 70 cm wide path is made around a circular garden having a diameter of 14 metres. What is the area of the path (in m<sup>2</sup>)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of a circular path of width w outside a circle of radius r is given by π × w × (2r + w).

Given width w = 70 cm = 0.7 m and inner radius r = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 m.

⇒ Area = π × 0.7 × (2 × 7 + 0.7)

⇒ Area = π × 0.7 × 14.7 = 10.29 π

∴ The correct answer is 10.29 π m2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of the circular garden = 14 m

Width of the path (w) = 70 cm = 0.7 m

Formula Used:

Area of circular ring = π × (R2 − r2)

Calculations:

⇒ Radius of the inner garden (r) = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 m

⇒ Radius of the outer circle (R) = 7 + 0.7 = 7.7 m

⇒ Area of the path = π × (7.72 − 72)

⇒ Area of the path = π × (7.7 − 7) × (7.7 + 7)

⇒ Area of the path = π × 0.7 × 14.7

⇒ Area of the path = 10.29 π m2

∴ The correct answer is 10.29 π m2.

Additional Information

Area of a Circular Ring

The area enclosed between two concentric circles of radii R and r (where R > r) is given by π(R2 − r2).

Path Inside a Circle

If a path of width w is constructed inside a circular garden of radius R, the area of the path becomes π × w × (2R − w).

Length of Arc and Area of Sector

questions.question: The average of 28 numbers is 52.5. The average of the first 12 numbers is 48.8 and that of the next 13 numbers is 45.8. If the other 3 numbers are excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.questionHtml: The average of 28 numbers is 52.5. The average of the first 12 numbers is 48.8 and that of the next 13 numbers is 45.8. If the other 3 numbers are excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

We only need the combined average of the first 12 and next 13 numbers (total 25 numbers). The 28 numbers data is a distractor.

Let the assumed average of these 25 numbers be 45.8.

Deviation of the first 12 numbers = 48.8 − 45.8 = +3.0

Net deviation on total average = (12 × +3.0) ÷ 25 = +1.44

Required Average = Assumed Average + Net deviation = 45.8 + 1.44 = 47.24

∴ The correct answer is 47.24.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average of first 12 numbers = 48.8

Average of next 13 numbers = 45.8

If the remaining 3 numbers are excluded, we just need to find the combined average of the first 12 numbers and the next 13 numbers (Total = 25 numbers).

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of the first 12 numbers = 12 × 48.8 = 585.6

⇒ Sum of the next 13 numbers = 13 × 45.8 = 595.4

⇒ Total sum of these 25 numbers = 585.6 + 595.4 = 1181

⇒ Average of the remaining 25 numbers = Total sum ÷ Total count

⇒ Average = 1181 ÷ 25

⇒ Average = 47.24

∴ The correct answer is 47.24.

Additional Information

Combined Average

If two groups have sizes n1 and n2 with averages A1 and A2 respectively, their combined average is given by: (n1 × A1 + n2 × A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Redundant Data Trap

In many competitive exam questions, extra data (like the overall average of 28 numbers here) is deliberately provided to trick candidates into lengthy and unnecessary calculations. Analyzing the final objective helps bypass this.

Deviation Method for Averages

Select a base assumed average (typically the lowest average value). Calculate the net sum of variations for all differing terms, divide by the total number of items, and adjust the assumed average by adding or subtracting this final net deviation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. The architect said that if the foundation were stronger, they could add two more floors, but as it stood, it was impossible .

Key Points

  • The sentence in the question is a **second conditional**, which is used to describe hypothetical situations in the present or future.
  • The sentence retains the second conditional structure even when transformed into indirect speech.
  • In the second conditional, the structure is: **If + past simple, would + base verb**.
  • In indirect speech, there is no change in the tense of the conditional clause, as the hypothetical situation remains true to the original statement.

Additional Information

    • Option 4: Incorrect. It mixes elements of the third conditional ("had been stronger") and second conditional, which is inconsistent with the original sentence.
  • Key Characteristics of Conditional Sentences:
    • 1st Conditional: Real or possible situations in the future (If + Present Simple, will + base verb).
    • 2nd Conditional: Hypothetical situations in the present or future (If + Past Simple, would + base verb).
    • 3rd Conditional: Unreal past situations (If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle).

Key Points
  • Option 1: Competitive use involves the transparent placement of advertisements, whereas proprietary misuse involves the use of "go out and vote" reminders to increase general turnout.

  • Option 2: Technology is democratic when used as a symmetrical medium for rival messaging, but becomes a threat when platform owners exercise asymmetrical, non-transparent control over information flow.

    • This is incorrect. The author does not claim superiority of billboards; they use billboards as an analogy for competitive transparency, not legal adjudication.
  • Option 4: Social media only becomes a threat to democracy when one candidate possesses significantly more followers than their opponent, thereby destroying the competitive balance.
    • This is incorrect. The author emphasizes misuse by platform owners, not follower counts, as the real danger to democracy.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Additional Information

  • Option 3: Misleading; billboards are used as analogy, not claimed superior.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'dissimilar to.'

Key Points

  • The phrase 'different like' is incorrect in this context.
  • The meaning of the word 'dissimilar' is not the same; different.
  • ​The preposition 'to' should be used after the word 'dissimilar.'
    • Example: His methods were not dissimilar to those used by Freud.
  • ​Therefore, the use of 'different like' should be replaced by 'dissimilar to'​ to make it grammatically correct.
  • ​​Correct sentence: The situation you’re in is not dissimilar to mine.

Additional Information    

  • Subject pronouns are pronouns that replace the subject in the sentence. 
  • The subject pronouns are we, you, he, she, it, and they.
  • Object pronouns do not replace the subject.
  • Instead, an object pronoun would replace the object in the sentence.
  • The object is the part of the sentence that is being done to, from or with the action.
  • The object pronouns are me, you, him, her, it, us, and them.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate preposition for the given blank. Being wrong opens us ______ the possibility of change.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate preposition for the given blank.

Being wrong opens us ______ the possibility of change.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1'.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "opens us up to" is a common collocation, meaning to expose us to or make us receptive to something. In this case, it means being wrong makes us open to the possibility of change.
  • "Up to" is the correct preposition to use in this context, as it implies the opening or revealing of possibilities.
  • The other prepositions, "into," "with," and "of to," do not fit the meaning or structure of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Complete Sentence: "Being wrong opens us up to the possibility of change."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "into" is incorrect because "into" typically implies a motion or direction, and here it does not convey the idea of opening up to possibilities.
  • Option 3: "with" is incorrect because "with" suggests being accompanied by something or someone, which does not fit the intended meaning of the sentence.
  • Option 4: "of to" is incorrect because this preposition combination is grammatically incorrect and does not make sense in the context of the sentence.

    • C follows sentence A as it is talking about a loud sound that came due to the car accident while everyone was sleeping.
    • B is the next sentence as it is describing the sight of the car accident.
    • D is the last sentence and forms a pair with sentence 6 as it means that after the occupants of both the cars shouted for help, people came out of their houses to help them.

Thus, the correct order is ACBD:

  • 1: Night before the zonal debate competition, I was practising my part till late at night.
  • A: Everyone was fast asleep and even I was planning to sleep. 
  • C: Suddenly, there was a loud crash and I jumped out of my bed and rushed out to see the cause of that sound.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first sentence (S1) is in the correct order, the sentences below it jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

S1. A man was on his way to the next village.

A.  It was not possible for him to go across before nightfall.

B. As evening fell, he found himself close to a river.

C. So, he decided to wait till daybreak and then continue his journey.

D. He found a place under a tree and lay down to sleep.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BACD".

Key Points

  •  Here S1 is the sentence that establishes the subject matter. It speaks about the travel of the man to the next village.
  • The sentence that follows S1 is B. On his travel to the village sentence B describes where he reached during the evening. Hence sentence B is the continuation of sentence S1.
  • After establishing that the man reaches the river, the next sentence explains that he was unable to cross the river before nightfall. So the sentence that follows B is A.
  • The next sentence adds the final decision taken by the man as to wait till daybreak and to continue his journey. And also sentence A and sentence C are connected. So the sentence that follows A is C.
  • Finally, the last sentence is D. 
  • Thus the final sequence is "BACD".
  • Hence the correct answer is Option 2.
